audience.programmeDescription: Archaeology at Leiden studies past societies through material remains, landscapes and heritage. It combines historical interpretation, scientific and digital analysis, artefact studies and practical fieldwork. Students entering from September 2026 follow a general programme without formal specialisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the published material does not establish the full curriculum for the new entrant cohort. The supported components are shown below. UCR offers relevant archaeology, heritage and research courses; the curriculum gap is not a conclusion that no suitable UCR response exists.

curriculum.limitation: This list contains 90 EC: the first-year 60 EC and 30 EC of approved elective space. The remaining compulsory 90 EC, including later course choices, internship and thesis allocation, still require cohort-specific clarification. It is not a complete 180-EC degree pathway.

componentNotes.arch1-06: Field Techniques includes mandatory practical attendance and archaeological recording exercises.
componentNotes.arch1-12: Field School requires passed Field Techniques and Natural Landscapes and attendance at the additional zero-credit Active Bystander training. The field practical and reports are assessed.
componentNotes.arch-open-30: 30 EC of recognised minor, exchange or approved elective study, without overlap with compulsory courses. A self-composed package needs coherence and at least 10 EC at level 300 or higher. Exchange requires a passed first year, a complementary programme and no study delay; applicable approval conditions apply.
